results.summary: Verified every field against the current official text of 247 CMR 6.00 and 247 CMR 20.00 (mass.gov PDFs, inflated and read in the browser, zero stream-decode failures) and against 21 CFR 1301.51 and 1301.52 on eCFR. The section's central architecture holds exactly: 247 CMR 6.00 contains precisely three "may not ... until it receives approval from the Board" prohibitions, and they are in 6.15(1), 6.15(2) and 6.16, with only 6.16 attaching a day count (at least 90 days, "unless otherwise approved by the Board"). The notice family is stated correctly and in the right direction: 6.12 runs 14 days forward from a change in the operating name and reaches nothing else; 6.11(1) and 6.11(2) each run 14 days backward and are owed independently; 6.14(1) runs 14 days backward by certified mail and 6.14(2) adds a 14-day waiting period, a transfer-date inventory of Schedules II through V plus reportable Schedule VI, dual Manager of Record signatures, a ten-day attestation from both pharmacies, two-year readily retrievable retention and the flat bar in 6.14(2)(f). The section's most easily doubted quotation is right: the second sentence of 6.11(1) does read "shall comply with 247 CMR 6.12 and 247 CMR 6.13 pertaining to closing a pharmacy and distributing controlled substances", and the section reports it as written rather than silently repairing the cross-reference while still sending the reader to 6.14 for the stock. The Manager of Record analysis is correct on both limbs: 6.10 states no deadline and contains no bar on the change taking effect first, and 247 CMR 20.05(1) supplies 14 calendar days running forward from the resignation, termination or change, with the application expressly satisfying it, alongside the personal duty in 20.05(3); the 30-day reports in 20.06(6)(e) and 20.07(2) are stated with the right triggers and the right filers. The two suitability lists are distinguished accurately: 6.03 has eleven factors framed as reaching "an applicant, licensee, or interest holder", includes prescriptive privileges at (9) as a status and professional-licence discipline and consent agreements at (10) and (11), and states no look-back; 6.10(3) has ten factors every one of which begins "A proposed Manager of Record", adds "or managed" to the entity factors, carries the five-year Board-discipline factor at (h) and has no prescriptive-privileges item. The three filing lists in 6.15 and 6.16 are separated correctly, including the point that 6.15(3) asks for the counseling area and the Massachusetts-only transport security plan while 6.16 asks for neither, that 6.15(1) reaches five pharmacy types, 6.15(2) three and 6.15(4) four, and that four of the 6.15(4) items are qualified "as" or "if applicable". The federal limbs match 21 CFR 1301.51 and 1301.52 clause for clause, including the "in person or by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested" channel, the 14-day period and its only escape (a waiver by the Special Agent in Charge), the single transfer-date inventory serving as final and initial, order forms for Schedules I and II, and the return of the certificate and unexecuted order forms on a discontinuance without a transfer. All five listed practice questions (MA-Q-0361, 0362, 0386, 0387, 0390) are answerable from the section and none is contradicted by it. The single defect found is a Low-severity citation placement in one quick_review bullet.

findings.problem: The section carries 247 CMR 6.13(6)(b)'s citation to "21 CFR 1307.21" forward without noting that no such section exists in the current CFR: part 1307 now runs 1307.01, .02, .03, .11, .13, .14, .15, .22, .31 and .41, disposal having moved to 21 CFR part 1317. ma_vs_federal[0] then characterises the attestation as demanding "proof that the federal route was followed", which leaves the live federal disposal route unnamed at that point.
findings.rationale: Not a misstatement of Massachusetts law: 6.13(6)(b) does cite 1307.21, the section reports the Board's requirement faithfully rather than silently substituting a different citation, and it separately and correctly routes the stock to 21 CFR part 1317 through 21 CFR 1301.52(c) (comparison_tables[4].rows[1] and decision_logic[5]). A candidate answering a Massachusetts question about what the closure attestation must say is therefore given the right answer. Recorded as Low because a one-clause note that the cited federal section has been superseded by part 1317 would be an improvement, not a correction.

results.summary: Verified every field against the current official text of 247 CMR 6.13 and 6.14 (mass.gov PDF, inflated and read in the browser, zero stream-decode failures) and against 21 CFR 1301.52 and part 1307 on eCFR. The six particulars in 6.13(1)(a)-(f) are listed correctly and in order, and the section's central teaching point - that (e) verifies customer notice already given and (f) states the intended controlled-substance procedure, so the three closure duties run in parallel rather than in sequence - is a sound reading of the text. The type-by-type table is right at every cell I could test: 6.13(2) drops exactly the controlled substance registration number, the Manager of Record's name and the disposal-or-transfer statement; 6.13(3) names five compounding types and does not name a non-resident Drug Store Pharmacy; 6.13(4)'s last sentence puts the Massachusetts-patient duty on the three non-resident types; 6.13(6) closes with "The provisions in 247 CMR 6.13(6) shall not apply to non-resident pharmacies"; and 6.13(7) names 6.13(3) and 6.13(4) and nothing else, so the section is right that the certified notice, the file-transfer duty and the post-closure submission survive for an institutional sterile compounding pharmacy. The clocks are correctly directed: 6.13(1), (2) and (3) and 6.14(1) each run backward and each carries "unless otherwise authorized by the Board", 6.13(4)'s 14 days carries no such qualifier and its 90 days is a look-back rather than a deadline, and 6.13(6) is indeed the only clock in 6.13 running forward from closure. The 6.14 walk-through matches (1)(a)-(h) and (2)(a)-(f) exactly, including the Schedules II through VI transfer class against the Schedules II through V plus reportable Schedule VI inventory class, the ten-day dual attestation, the two-year readily retrievable retention and 6.14(2)(f)'s absolute bar on post-transfer possession; the worked example's arithmetic (notice day 1, earliest transfer day 15, attestation due day 25) is right, and the observation that where the stock moves on or before the closure date the ten-day transfer attestation ordinarily falls due before the 14-day closure attestation is correct. The federal limb matches 21 CFR 1301.52(a)-(e) clause for clause, and the section correctly keeps the controlled substances registration surrendered to the Board apart from the DEA certificate of registration returned under 1301.52(c). All four listed practice questions (MA-Q-0072, 0074, 0363, 0385) are answerable from the section and none is contradicted by it. The single finding is the Low-severity point that the section repeats 6.13(6)(b)'s citation to 21 CFR 1307.21, a section that no longer exists in the CFR, without flagging it.
